verdict: The huge translucent navy ellipse and pale-blue upper arc are procedural ActionPanel decoration drawn by OperaCareerWorld2D._draw_activity_focus. They are not baked into any Hall backdrop and do not own input. The same callback also draws a seven-pearl generic progress trail, so removing the entire callback globally would discard useful behavior and affect careers outside the Hall.

construction: 1253-1259: action_panel is a transparent ColorRect, mouse_filter IGNORE, and its draw signal connects to _draw_activity_focus.

1978-1993: _draw_activity_focus computes centre = action_panel.size * (0.5, 0.48), radius = max(width,height) * 0.52, scales drawing by (1.0,0.62), draws two filled circles and one upper arc, then resets the draw transform.
1994-2014: the same callback draws seven progress pearls from phase_fill.value. Chapter 2 CandyMaker/Detective drawing branches also live here but are outside this Hall scope.
exact_owner.declared_purpose: The source comment calls the shapes a soft theatre-light bloom behind themed minigame art and the pearl trail the only generic progress information.
exact_owner.input_ownership: The ActionPanel itself ignores mouse input. Its child OperaGestureSurface or OperaBalletSurface owns the phase gesture and local cues. Removing only decorative draw calls cannot change hit regions or gesture callbacks.
not_the_owner: OperaWorldBackdrop2D._draw_spotlights draws two translucent trapezoid beams from the top of the canvas; those beams are separately visible in the captures but do not form the ellipse/arc.
The stage_* 2x2 backdrop tiles contain the painted stage, proscenium and floor. Native tile inspection does not contain this procedural ellipse/arc.
OperaGestureSurface's generic hold ring is a separate mode-local circle and OperaBalletSurface owns its portrait shells and demo pointer.

ballerina_stage.layout_source: _apply_panel_layout at 2741-2745; _performance_stage_layout retains this specialist panel geometry
ballerina_stage.effect: The bloom covers most of the right activity canvas, including the mirror target and pose choices. Its oversized geometry is a direct result of using the larger dimension for radius before applying a fixed vertical squash.

magician_and_popstar_stage.effect: The bloom masks the central value structure behind the phase props; the cyan arc crosses the upper part of the central action area.

observed_geometry.practice: The same callback runs when ActionPanel is visible in practice. Ordinary cards use 416x292 with a 392x232 child surface; Ballerina uses its larger 874x680 specialist canvas. The stage-only evidence below does not independently score the practice bloom.

redraw_sources: Phase/widget binding and restore queue ActionPanel redraw at 2642.
Special full-canvas and specialist layout branches queue redraw at 2715, 2727, 2749 and 2769; ordinary layout queues at 2779.
Gesture/result updates queue ActionPanel redraw during active play, including 3421 and 3572.
The callback executes only while ActionPanel is visible; bop, lens and talk phases hide it at 2752-2755.
all_runtime_callers_and_visibility.career_filter: _draw_activity_focus currently returns only for Teacher, Geologist and active Racer driving. Therefore the bloom applies to all other visible ActionPanels, including every visible Ballerina, Magician and Pop Star phase; this report recommends no change outside those three Hall careers.
phase_specific_layers_preserved: OperaBalletSurface._draw owns mirror portraits, shells, pose selection, round progress pearls, demo pointer and completion halo.
OperaGestureSurface._draw owns Magician and Pop Star phase objects, generic hold/swipe/circle/choice cues, demo finger and completion feedback.
OperaPerformanceOverlay owns the top practice/stage status and player/rival progress bars for these two-act careers.

capture_evidence.observed: The large navy bloom and cyan arc wash over the right-side pose canvas and mirror target.
The 520x322 computed ellipse sits behind the lamb, cabinet, hat and wand and masks the painted central floor.
The same ellipse/arc is visible behind the microphone and dance pads and reads as a separate system layer.

claims: Ballerina observations call the large translucent navy gesture arc a system overlay that washes over the room and target.
Magician observations say the navy arc masks the central stage value structure.
The shared priority is to replace or substantially constrain the oversized navy gesture arc before mounted recapture.
existing_review_evidence.limit: The independent review is based on configured desktop Mobile stills for the first source phase. It does not establish touch behavior, phone readability, later phases or natural navigation.

scoped_options.name: Hall bloom removal with progress retained
scoped_options.change_boundary: Inside _draw_activity_focus, skip only the three ellipse/arc draw calls when career_id is ballerina, magician or popstar. Continue into the existing custom branches and seven-pearl progress code.
preserves: phase-local visual hints and demo pointers
scoped_options.why_preferred: It removes the exact independently observed weak layer with the smallest behavior surface. No fallback art or new asset is introduced.
scoped_options.risk: The phase art loses the intended dark contrast bloom; recapture must verify props remain legible against all three practice and stage paintings.

scoped_options.name: Stage-only Hall bloom removal
scoped_options.change_boundary: Skip the three ellipse/arc calls only when career_id is in the Hall set and _performance_on_stage() is true; retain current practice bloom and all pearls.
scoped_options.why_consider: It exactly matches the three cited stage captures and avoids changing uncaptured practice composition.
scoped_options.risk: The same Ballerina large-panel formula applies during practice, and practice captures may show the same defect. This option could leave a known-looking inconsistency across the act transition.

scoped_options.name: Constrain bloom to a smaller neutral floor pool
scoped_options.change_boundary: For the Hall set only, cap bloom radius using the smaller panel dimension and reduce the vertical extent/alpha; keep the progress pearls unchanged.
scoped_options.risk: A fixed smaller ellipse still lacks phase-object ownership and may remain a synthetic overlay. Ballerina targets occupy multiple separate portrait bounds, so a single pool cannot follow the true active target without adding cross-surface coupling. This has more tuning risk than removal.

scoped_options.name: Suppress entire generic focus callback for Hall
scoped_options.change_boundary: Return early for the three Hall careers.
scoped_options.risk: Magician and Pop Star lose the seven-pearl generic progress trail. Even though the top performance bar remains, removing redundant progress feedback is broader than the proven visual defect. This should not be the first implementation.

do_not_do: Do not remove _draw_activity_focus globally; its callback serves other careers and Chapter 2 custom drawings.
Do not hide or disable ActionPanel to remove the bloom; its children own the actual gesture surface.
Do not treat OperaWorldBackdrop2D spotlights as the ellipse owner or remove them as a substitute fix.
Do not replace the overlay with a generic fallback card. Preserve the phase-specific painted props and local instructional cues.
Do not alter stage tiles, actor assets, touch geometry, goals, progress accounting or two-act semantics for this repair.
required_followup: After an implementation is separately authorized, capture the same three stage states and corresponding practice states at Mobile 1280x720 with unchanged input coordinates.
Verify local target highlights, demo finger, hold/circle/swipe cues and progress remain visible without the bloom.
Verify Magician pale props and Pop Star microphone/notes retain contrast on their painted backgrounds.
Run parser/inference and focused Hall interaction probes; still review remains separate from phone, child and owner acceptance.
acceptance_limits: This identifies source ownership and proposes scope boundaries; it does not visually accept a repaired state.
Only three named run01 stage captures were directly inspected for this trace.
No full-Hall, game-wide, motion, touch, target-device, child, owner or release acceptance is claimed.
